name: Scrapgospel Pilgrim's Patchwork Shroud
description:
A full-length outer garment assembled from at least forty distinct fabric salvages — factory floor insulation, transit seat upholstery, synthetic fur scraps, acid-bleached cargo tarp — stitched together in a deliberate mandala pattern centered on the back. Practitioners of the Shelf-born Meridian Drift faith wear this as both devotional garment and survival layer. Embroidered circuit diagrams intersperse with hand-painted deity glyphs drawn from a syncretized mix of Yoruba, Shinto, and Orthodox iconography, all reinterpreted through a post-corporate lens.

Each shroud is unique, assembled over years, and added to after significant life events. The hem drags deliberately — a statement that the wearer is not running from anything.
functionality: Layered construction provides genuine thermal insulation against Shelf acid rain. The outer tarp-fabric layer repels light chemical exposure. Deep interior pockets are sewn into the lining at devotional intervals — each holds a small sacred object.
what_it_says: This person carries their entire spiritual history on their back and answers to no corponation's calendar.
worn_by: DIY anti-corporate artists using faith as framework
story_hooks: A shroud surfaces at a Tier 4 auction house — someone sold a dead elder's devotional garment, and the community wants it back.
One of the embroidered circuit diagrams is a functional schematic for something that shouldn't exist on the Shelf.
A new Meridian Drift convert is being pressured to burn their shroud as proof of corporate loyalty — they refuse.
